summary: Both sides are Nyan Cat drawn as a strict 2-frame loop, but the original is a fixed 300-pixel (60 wide x 5 tall) sprite look-up table while the port is a resolution-independent square-canvas sprite, so on the manifest rig (grid 16x16) the original wraps into an illegible colour mosaic while the port draws a crisp 16x16 cat, and on the original's native 60x5 geometry the roles invert.
observations: Rigs/health: manifest default rig is grid 16x16 (256 px). Both sides compile and run there with no runtime error. Neither side exposes any control (meta.json sides.orig.controls == [] and sides.port.controls == []), so there is no control-surface mismatch and no dialed comparison is possible.

ORIGINAL IS INDEX-ONLY (1D as far as our engine is concerned). Its flat pixel sequence at grid 12x12 (144 px) is byte-identical to the first 144 entries of its grid 16x16 sequence (144/144 match, labels dump-a vs dump12), and identical again on --rig strip --pixels 256. Its output at pixel i is therefore a pure function of (i, t) with no x/y or pixelCount dependence.

PORT IS (x,y)-DRIVEN AND RESOLUTION-INDEPENDENT. Only 43/144 pixels match between its 12x12 and 16x16 renders, and its mean brightness stays ~47-57 across 8x8, 12x12, 16x16, 20x20, 24x24, 32x32, 40x24 and 48x48 — i.e. it scales the sprite to fill whatever canvas it is given.

Numeric proof of the 1D/2D split at 16x16, t=0: mean |RGB| difference between index i and i+1 vs between i and i+16 is orig 83.7 vs 259.8 (ratio 3.1 — a smooth 1D ribbon that ignores row boundaries), port 67.8 vs 102.2 (ratio 1.5 — genuinely 2D-coherent).

THE ORIGINAL'S NATIVE GEOMETRY IS 60 x 5 = 300 PIXELS. Repeated 6-pixel motifs in the original's flat sequence recur at exact index gaps of 60 (e.g. yellow+5xpink at indices 46, 106, 226; grey+pink/red face motif at 67 and 127), and the original renders cleanly at exactly 300 px and no more: 256 px OK, 289 px (17x17) OK, 300 px (60x5) OK, 324 px (18x18) RUNTIME ERR 'array index out of bounds', likewise 400/576/960/1024/2304 px. The port has no such ceiling and renders fine at all of those counts.

Reshaped/rendered at 60x5 the ORIGINAL is a legible Nyan Cat scene: row0 an 8-px yellow bar at cols 5-12 plus a yellow-bracketed 10-px pink block at cols 46-55 (pop-tart top); rows 1-3 a grey/pink/red cat-face cluster at cols 2-15, a rainbow trail across cols 16-45 stacked red/orange (row1), orange/yellow/yellow-green (row2), green/blue (row3) with a square-wave step edge every 4 columns, and the pink pop-tart body at cols 46-55; row4 a yellow bar at cols 4-15, blue blocks at 16-27 and grey paw pixels at 45-58.

The PORT at 60x5 collapses to unreadable horizontal bars (row1 red/orange, row2 orange/cyan/grey, row3 solid orange, rows 0 and 4 black) — its square sprite squashed into 5 rows. So there is NO rig on which both sides look right at once.

On the manifest rig (16x16) the PORT draws an unmistakable pixel-art Nyan Cat occupying rows 2-12 only (rows 0-1 and 13-15 fully black): orange crust (255,137,0) around a pink pop-tart (255,140,174) with magenta dot texture (229,34,116) at cols 1-7, grey cat body/head (71,67,62) with dark eye/mouth pixels at cols 8-12, a 6-band rainbow trail at cols 8-15 (255,0,0 / 255,114,0 / 234,255,0 / 5,255,0 / 0,178,255 / 173,0,255), and two pairs of grey paw pixels on row 12.

On the same 16x16 rig the ORIGINAL is the 60-stride ribbon wrapped onto 16 columns, so features run across row boundaries (e.g. a 10-px pink run starting at row2 col14 and continuing through row3 col7). A viewer sees yellow bars on rows 0 and 15, scattered pink/grey chunks, and coarse red->orange->yellow->green->blue banding across rows 4-14 — nyan-ish colours but no cat.

Palette census at 16x16, t=0 (256 px). Orig: 12 distinct colours, 64 black (25%), grey75 (76,75,73) x38, pink (255,127,127) x34, yellow (255,214,0) x28, orange (255,152,0) x16, green (51,255,0) x16, spring-green (0,255,101) x16, red (255,0,0) x14, yellow-green (188,255,0) x14, red (255,25,25) x7, blue (50,0,255) x7. Port: 14 distinct colours, 134 black (52%), orange (255,137,0) x24, grey (71,67,62) x27, pink (255,140,174) x16, red x11, orange (255,114,0) x11, magenta (229,34,116) x9, yellow x7, green x6, cyan-blue x3, purple x3.

Colour differences that survive the geometry difference: the original's rainbow is an evenly-spaced hue ramp that STOPS AT BLUE (50,0,255) with no violet/purple and no cyan, and it uses a single desaturated pink (255,127,127) for the pop-tart with no dot texture and no separate crust colour. The port's rainbow is the canonical 6-colour nyan flag INCLUDING purple (173,0,255) and cyan-blue (0,178,255), and it has three distinct pop-tart colours (crust/body/dots).

Coverage/brightness: the original lights 190/256 px (74%) and averages meanBrightness 89 (meanR/G/B 122/104/41); the port lights 122/256 px (48%) and averages 56.5 (89/51/29). The original is ~1.6x brighter overall and fills the rig; the port leaves half of it black.

MOTION: both sides are STRICT TWO-FRAME LOOPS. Dumping every 0.05 s over 0-1.2 s and again in four windows spread over 0-34 s, each side shows exactly 2 distinct frames and nothing else (orig state sequence 000011111000011111..., port 0000111100001111...). Neither scrolls, drifts or cycles a palette; the survey sheet at 0 s and 59.9 s is identical on both sides.
CADENCE: at the default 20 fps the original holds each state 5 frames (0.25 s) for a 0.5 s cycle; the port holds each state 4 frames (0.2 s) for a 0.4 s cycle — the port's loop is 25% faster.

FRAME-RATE COUPLING (mild, on the ORIGINAL). Measured by state-transition times, not the motion stat: orig cycle period is 0.6 s at 10 fps, 0.5 s at 20 fps, 0.45 s at 40 fps — i.e. 0.4 s plus two frame intervals of latency, so the original converges on 0.4 s only as fps rises. The port is a clean 0.4 s at 10, 20 and 40 fps. So the port matches the original's asymptotic rate but not its rate at any realistic frame rate.

STEADY STATE: both sides are stable. Over --seconds 120 --fps 4 and over --skip 120 --seconds 12 --fps 20 the stats are unchanged from t=0 (orig meanBrightness avg 89 min 87 max 91, port 56.5/56/57), brightnessTrend 'steady' on both, no decay, no saturation, no freeze.
DETERMINISM: seeds 1, 7 and 1234 produce byte-identical t=0 frames on BOTH sides — neither pattern is random-driven, so the stochastic-character caveat does not apply.

The high zeroMotionFrames counts (orig 96/120, port 91/120 in baseline) are NOT a freeze — they are the 2-frame loop's hold periods; motionLit peaks at 58.1 (orig) and 60.3 (port) on the transition frames.
feedback: GEOMETRY IS THE HEADLINE BUG. The original is a fixed 300-pixel look-up table laid out as 60 columns x 5 rows and indexed by pixel index alone — it produces the same colour at index i no matter what rig it is on, and it hard-fails ('array index out of bounds') above 300 pixels. The port instead rasterizes a sprite from normalized (x,y) into whatever canvas it is given. Rebuild the port as a 60-wide, 5-tall index-addressed sprite so that pixel i gets the colour of sprite cell (i mod 60, floor(i / 60)); that single change is what makes the two agree on any rig.

Target scene layout to reproduce, read off the original at 60x5: rainbow trail occupying columns 16-45 as horizontal bands (row1 red then orange, row2 orange/yellow/yellow-green, row3 green then blue, row4 blue at cols 16-27), with the trail's leading edge stepping up/down in 4-column blocks (a square wave, not a smooth diagonal); pink pop-tart body as a 10x4 block at columns 46-55 rows 0-3 bracketed by single yellow pixels; grey cat cluster with pink/red face detail at columns 0-15 rows 1-4; grey paw pixels on row 4 at columns 45-58; yellow bars on row 0 cols 5-12 and row 4 cols 4-15.

PALETTE. Drop the purple (173,0,255) and cyan-blue (0,178,255) from the trail — the original's ramp is an even hue sweep that ends at blue (50,0,255): red (255,0,0) and (255,25,25), orange (255,152,0), yellow (255,214,0), yellow-green (188,255,0), green (51,255,0), spring-green (0,255,101), blue (50,0,255). Use a single flat pink (255,127,127) for the pop-tart with NO magenta dot texture and NO separate orange crust — the original has neither. Cat grey is (76,75,73).

BRIGHTNESS/COVERAGE. On the manifest 16x16 rig the original lights 74% of pixels at mean brightness 89; the port lights 48% at 56.5. Once the 60x5 layout is right this should follow automatically, but check it: the original leaves only ~25% of its 300 cells black, the port currently leaves ~52% black.

ANIMATION. Keep the strict 2-frame loop (both sides already do this correctly — 2 distinct frames and nothing else over 34 s, no scrolling, no palette walk). Slow it from 0.4 s per cycle to 0.5 s per cycle at 20 fps (0.25 s per frame). Note the original's period is frame-rate coupled (0.6 s at 10 fps, 0.5 s at 20 fps, 0.45 s at 40 fps ~= 0.4 s + 2 frame intervals); matching the 20 fps number is the practical target, matching the +2-frame latency exactly is optional polish.

The difference between the two animation frames in the original is small and local: the trail's step edges shift by one pixel and the yellow bars lose/gain a pixel at their ends (e.g. row0's yellow run goes 8 px -> 7 px, and the cat-face motif shifts one column). It is a bob/wiggle of the trail, not a translation of the whole scene.

MANIFEST NOTE FOR WHOEVER OWNS THE RIG TABLE: grid 16x16 is not this pattern's native geometry. The original wants 60x5 (300 px) exactly. Re-judging this pair after a fix would be far more informative on --rig grid --grid 60x5.
Neither side has any controls, so nothing to add or remove on the dial surface.
